body:
I could not reproduce this on my other device. 
System information:
Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated Radeon RX 580 Series (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21923.1000) - AMD Ryzen 7 2700X Eight-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.94 GiB memory

It's still reproducible on my Intel PC. I don't know enough about how shader caches work to confidently say why switching between 32/64-bit works fine on the AMD (without manually clearing the cache), but on the Intel it crashes under the same conditions.
Considering the intel doesn't need to clear the cache when launched with rendering_method forward_plus (or mobile) I think it's an issue with gl_compatibility, and what changes when going from 32-bit -> 64-bit (Since 64-bit -> 32-bit works fine.)
I'm still not sure why those changes would only be an issue with Intel though. (Or why the cache wouldn't be regenerated between versions. 👀)

It seems similar to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104484#issuecomment-3571153451 since that's only reproducible on the Intel PC as well, but since that issue exists in all of the rendering methods it's probably not directly related.

**Update**:
Earlier I realized that the driver tool that Intel provides only lists OEM-approved drivers, and the latest driver those displayed were around 4 months older than the latest generic driver.

After I located & installed the generic drivers manually the issue I linked in my previous comment was resolved, but it didn't fix this issue. Despite that I still think it's an issue with Intel devices since I couldn't replicate it on AMD, but until an update rolls out to fix whatever causes this interaction to happen I'll keep this issue open.

Another solution may be to have Godot automatically clear the shader cache and then regenerate it whenever a switch between the 32-bit & 64-bit editor is detected, but I'm not sure if there's a reason that doesn't already happen or not.
